sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that even the revelation of light related to worlds before the first contraction involves prior contractions, and the purpose of the Torah is to draw down the light before all contractions, up to the level of Atzmus.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that what is stated in the maamar
(at its beginning24)
that the intention in the giving of the Torah is to draw down the Ein Sof that is before the contraction,

even though the superiority of the Torah is that even within the Ein Sof that is before the contraction itself, the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is above the light that relates to worlds is drawn down,
it is,
because also the drawing down of the light that relates to worlds
(that is before the contraction)
is through contraction.
For even though the contraction that occurred in this light
(that relates to worlds)
is called the first contraction,
nevertheless it is explained elsewhere25
that even before the first contraction there were several contractions.
For in addition to the fact that the drawing down of light that relates to worlds from the light that is above relation to worlds is through contraction as above,
behold, also the drawing down of the light that is above relation to worlds is through contraction.
For since this light as well
(that is above relation to worlds)
is in the category of drawing down and revelation,
and before this it was included in the Atzmus of the Luminary itself,26
[and in particular it can be said that this explanation that it was included in the Atzmus of the Luminary itself means that it was included in the Atzmus that is above27
the description of light28],
it is therefore understood29,
that the drawing down of the light that is in the category of revelation from the light that is included in the Atzmus of the Luminary is through an immense contraction.
And based on this it can be said that what is stated in the maamar that the intention in the giving of the Torah is to draw down the light that is before the contraction — the intention in this is
(not only for the light before the first contraction, but)
also for the light that is before all contractions.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies that the maamar's statement that Parshat HaChodesh was said immediately after the Exodus refers to after the telling of the Exodus in the Torah, highlighting the superiority of the Torah's revelation over the revelation of worlds as it appears in the Torah itself.

translations.translation: And based on this, it is also possible to explain what is stated in the maamar30
that Parshat HaChodesh was said immediately after the Exodus from Egypt,
for this is seemingly perplexing,
for it is explicit in the verse31
that Parshat HaChodesh was said in the land of Egypt,
and it can be said,
that what is stated in the maamar that Parshat HaChodesh was said after the Exodus from Egypt means after the saying and recounting of the Exodus from Egypt
(the Exodus from Egypt as it is in the Torah).
For after all the commands
(in the Torah)
were said to Pharaoh to send the children of Israel out of Egypt,
until the final warning of the plague of the firstborn, after which Pharaoh said "Go, you and all the people" etc.32,
behold, immediately after the saying of the Exodus from Egypt, Parshat HaChodesh was said.
And the explanation is,
that the superiority of the revelation of the Torah over the revelation of worlds
(explained in this maamar)
is also over the revelation of worlds as it is in the Torah.
For this is what the maamar brings from Rashi's statement, "The Torah should have begun only from 'This month is for you,' and what is the reason it began with Bereishis,"
that even the matter of "In the beginning He created"
(and likewise the narrative of the Patriarchs etc.33)
as it is in the Torah is only
(like)
an introduction to Parshat HaChodesh,
for this Parsha is the essential beginning of the Torah.
Therefore, also regarding the matter of the Exodus from Egypt, which is a preparation for the Giving of the Torah,
the maamar speaks about the matter of the Exodus from Egypt as it is in the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the superiority of the Torah's revelation to the level of Atzmus of Ein Sof before all contractions, explaining that the entire Torah preceded the world and that Parshat HaChodesh reveals the Atzmus of Ein Sof before all contractions.

translations.translation: And it is possible to connect this matter
[that the revelation of the Torah is higher even than the revelation of worlds as it is in the Torah]
with what was explained above
(section 4)
that the revelation of the Torah is the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is above all contractions
(even from the contractions that are before the first contraction),
based on the known principle that the entirety of the Torah
(even the narratives of the Torah that are before Parshat HaChodesh)
preceded the world,34
and since the beginning of the matter of the world is from the first contraction,35
the Torah that preceded the world is in the Ein Sof that is before the contraction.
And furthermore it can be said,
that since even in the light that is before the contraction there is already the beginning of the root of the measurement of worlds,
the Torah that preceded the world is in the light that is in the category of revelation to itself that is above relation to worlds.
For this is also the case regarding the narratives of the Torah that are before Parshat HaChodesh.
And the superiority of Parshat HaChodesh,
the essential beginning of the Torah,
is,
the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is before all contractions.
